questions.q: What does prompt assembly do in a RAG pipeline?
options: It turns the final, re-ranked list of chunks into the literal text a model reads
It generates the embedding vectors for new documents
It trains the embedding model on retrieved chunks
It deletes irrelevant chunks from the vector database
questions.explain: Prompt assembly takes the chunks that survived retrieval and re-ranking and formats them into the actual text sent to the model.

questions.q: In a Messages API request, where should the instruction 'answer only using the provided Context' live?
options: Nowhere — the model infers this automatically
In the max_tokens field
In the system field, separate from the retrieved data
In a separate API call made after the model responds
questions.explain: system carries the standing behavioral instruction for the whole request, kept separate from the per-request data (the retrieved chunks and question) in messages.

questions.q: What happens if a RAG prompt omits an explicit grounding instruction?
options: The model will refuse to answer entirely
The API request will fail with an error
The vector database will reject the query
A capable model may answer from its own training knowledge even when the retrieved chunks don't actually cover the question
questions.explain: Without being told to stay grounded in the Context, a model can answer correctly from memory even when retrieval didn't actually surface relevant chunks — undermining the point of RAG.

questions.q: Why are retrieved chunks numbered (like [1], [2]) during prompt assembly?
options: Numbering is purely cosmetic and has no functional purpose
It gives each chunk a stable label the model can refer back to later, enabling citations
It sets the order chunks are embedded in
It determines each chunk's similarity score
questions.explain: A chunk needs a stable label assigned at assembly time so the model's answer can reference a specific source — this can't be added after the model has already responded.

questions.q: What does giving the model explicit permission to say 'I don't know' accomplish in a grounding instruction?
options: It increases the model's max_tokens limit automatically
It makes the model skip the system field entirely
It allows an honest non-answer when retrieval genuinely comes up empty, instead of a guess
It forces the model to always retrieve additional chunks
questions.explain: Pairing the grounding instruction with permission to admit uncertainty is what makes an honest 'I don't know' possible when the retrieved context doesn't actually answer the question.
